reason: Selected cross-model benchmark results motivate direct coordination evaluation rather than assuming transfer from single-agent scores.

candidates.title: Evaluate coordination directly when selecting a team model
candidates.rule: When choosing models for multi-agent planning, include direct coordination evaluations instead of ranking candidates only by single-agent task scores.
candidates.passage: models with similar SA task performance often exhibit markedly different MA planning competence.
candidates.finding: Across Qwen and Llama generations, large single-agent gains accompany modest understanding gains and relatively flat multi-agent planning scores. The selection recommendation is inferred from observed score relationships.
workloads: Paper single-agent, multi-agent understanding and planning benchmark suite
candidates.conditions: Compare relevant partner interactions and roles; parameter count and generation are not causal interventions.
candidates.limitations: Observational benchmark comparisons do not prove scaling can never yield coordination. The inspected future training directions are proposals, not validated recipes.
candidates.validation_test: Compare candidate models on actual planner-executor or peer coordination tasks with fixed partners and budgets; test unfamiliar partners and failures alongside ordinary task accuracy.

review_scope: Selected abstract, introduction, methods or main-result sections; not a comprehensive paper or appendix review.
